description:
The StAyTB is made for high volume 650b up to 2.2″. With that info I am sure you can work out what other things might fit if you fancy.

The StAyTB is built with a modular dropout system that can take inserts for through axle (142 x 12), QR 135mm or horizontal SS/Fixed also at 135mm (although in this case the rear brake caliper position – use and effectiveness – is very much up to you). At some point soon we will also be offering a Stayer made (Hulsroy designed) UDH insert for the SRAM fam future bike peoples.

The gearing option is also hopefully practical and simple. We did not envisage the StAyTB to be the frame of someone looking from the outset to build with wireless tech, although you of course very much could if you wanted to as long as you don’t need any internal cables as the stAyTB doesn’t do internal cables. The gear routing therefore is for a front and rear mech with a trad STI adjuster and under BB routing arrangement. It will work with anything from one gear to loads of gears as long as you are either running mechanical something or fully wireless.

The breaks are ISO disc and the routing assumes full housing or hose and runs along the top of the top tube. Flat mount is an option with the correct adaptors but the frame is made for IS or post mount calipers with an IS adaptor.

Seat post is 27.2 and holds in place with a fancy fastback with removable threaded boss to save your frame in the event of a particularly enthusiastic occurance of over tightening. It takes an M6 bolt and barrel nut that can be obtained either from us or similarly hardware shops or workshop type places across the globe.

The headtube is for 1 1/8″ straight steerer forks – like ours! – or others with an axle to crown of around 395mm.

The frame has M5 bosses for fenders and a rack as well as a BSA bottom bracket for all options of crank attachment.

The logos are stickers not painted. Replacements as well as alternative colourways will be avaliable soon. The fancy headbadge, available as an additional, is attached with M3 screws on to the frame to make cleaning and future repainting easier. Without it the frame comes with a rather attractive headbadge sticker of the same design.

Reynolds steel fillet brazed frame. No filing, no fuss…a little fuss, but NO frivolity or tomfoolery! Constructed from stuff by the Stayer Workshop – for fun for ourselves and eventually for you; as well as for our livelihood :). I don’t like what I do every day but I do love what I do quite often and, as always, I hope those bits of it all come across in what we make and call a Stayer.

So! welcome the stAyTB, rare as hens teeth, filet o fish – and affectionate tongue in cheek – All Terrain Bicycle frame project with friends. I hope it is all that you desire, or that it is desired by all or it just tickles your tastebuds enough to welcome a smile. There is more than a little in the way of homage to bikes we love in here but I hope without parody or nostalgia. So, this is our Stayer mid life crisis bike number one. A town bike, if you like, for after school Sainsbugs (other supermarkets are available), bossing the shopping and jumping curbs. Feeling high about riding your bike and being a bit of a duuuude about it. But also! more capable a thing. For off roading or groading, taking a dusty roll out on in the gloaming instead of the smooth rolling, plush, like shiny shoes down the high road to Spoons. Mud flaps flapping, chain slapping, contemplating the one hand clapping and doing your thing.

Ok! enough! We haven’t just made this frame to look good and make you feel warm and fuzzy, ready to shreddy etc but also with good sense and some idea of what you might be doing with it or building it up with. Be you a bike jumble parts aficionado or in search of the simple life and a working solution from the quagmire of new bits, bobs, standards and randoms the internet of bike things has to provide. With luck this frame – and its options! – will cater for both the obsolete and the contemporary in equal measure.
